items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So we used to get together at the house and play.

ctx.x: the summer -- into the summer, I believe. And this was just before my sixteenth birthday. I guess it was about the middle of the summer. One of the fellows who had been playing in Booker Coleman's band had left the band, and went to... I think he had gotten this job in Annapolis, Maryland. And the next thing I knew, he was coming to my house saying that he wanted me to go to Annapolis with him, which was a long ways away to actually travel and play a job. That was just like going to heaven, you know. I really…

His name was Roosevelt Williams, a trumpet player. He had been coming to these jam sessions that I had been playing up there... Anyway, he took me. As I said, it was just before my sixteenth birthday. And he had another kid that was about 14 then, and he played saxophone and clarinet. His name was Oswald Gibson. And he took us down to Annapolis, Maryland, and I think we spent the month of August down there -- probably the latter part of July and August, until school opened again.

But that was another great experience. Down there I ran into situations of having to learn pieces fast. Down there was when I really realized that I couldn't read. You know, I knew what reading was about, but I had never had the experience of actually sitting up reading a piece of music --
